card: Configures Guix to build official Linux x86_64 and aarch64 release binaries (excluding GUI tools) as static position-independent executables (-static-pie) using glibc 2.44, resolving #19075. This allows bitcoind and command-line utilities to run without host dynamic linker dependencies on non-glibc distributions like Alpine Linux or distributions with older C libraries. The change patches glibc to eliminate non-deterministic Guix store paths and prevent NSS dlopen calls, which disables dynamic host resolution modules such as mDNS, LDAP, or SSSD. Guix symbol and security checking scripts are updated to verify static ELF binaries.
changed_since_previous: Added release notes detailing the portability improvements for Linux binaries and warning about disabled dynamic NSS name resolution.
evidence: PR description notes it fixes #19075 ('build: Investigate aarch64 pointer authentication').
Release note confirms release binaries for x86_64 and aarch64 Linux 'can now be run on non-glibc based systems, as well as on systems that ship with older glibcs than those previously supported'.
problem: Linux release binaries rely on host dynamic linkers and glibc versions, preventing them from running on non-glibc distributions like Alpine Linux or distributions with older glibc versions. Dynamic linking also impedes security hardening mitigations such as aarch64 pointer authentication.

risk.why: A flaw in the static toolchain or glibc patches could break official Linux release binaries across multiple distributions or cause runtime DNS and network resolution failures.

scope_notes: Touches Guix toolchains and package definitions, introduces glibc build patches to ensure build determinism and avoid dlopen, and adapts ELF symbol checking scripts for static binaries.
summary: Build official Linux x86_64 and aarch64 non-GUI executables (bitcoind and CLI tools) as static position-independent executables (-static-pie) using Guix and glibc 2.44. Patch glibc to strip non-deterministic Guix store paths and disable runtime dlopen in NSS modules. Update symbol-check and security-check scripts to validate static ELF executables and add release notes documenting the change.
